title: Six sum-free colours for 1..N (Schur numbers, S(6))
description: Colour every whole number from 1 to N with six colours so that no colour holds x, y and x + y (x = y allowed), for an N larger than the best known one. The checker tests a colouring in plain whole-number arithmetic.
objective: Colour each integer 1, 2, ..., N with one of 6 colours so that no colour contains numbers x, y and x + y (x = y allowed, so no colour may contain both x and 2x). Score: N. A valid colouring of 1..N shows S(6) >= N (OEIS A045652), equivalently f(6) = S(6) + 1 >= N + 1 (OEIS A030126).

bestKnown.quote: We give an explicit partition of {1, ..., 538} into six sum-free sets. This shows S(6) ≥ 538 and improves the bound S(6) ≥ 537 of Chen, Zhu and Long.
bestKnown.note: A preprint (its Zenodo page: 'Version v1.2.0 Preprint'), not peer reviewed. OEIS A045652 (revised 23 Oct 2026) still lists 537. best_known.json is the colouring of that preprint.

objectFormat: A JSON object {"k": 6, "N": <integer 1..5000>, "colours": [c_1, ..., c_N]} where c_i is an integer 0..5, the colour of the integer i. No other keys: an accepted object is shown publicly. At most 20,000 bytes as the result file carries it.
shows: That this one colouring splits 1..N into six sets with no x + y = z inside a set (x = y included), so S(6) is at least N. With N above the best known value, it is better than the value in the named source as of the date shown.
notCovered: Passing shows only that this one colouring of 1..N has no monochromatic x + y = z (x = y included), so S(6) >= N. It does not give the exact value of S(6), says nothing about the growth question listed as no. 483 in the Erdős problem database (is f(k) < c^k for some constant c?), and does not show that nobody found the same or a longer colouring earlier.
alsoBelongsAt: OEIS A045652 and A030126, the sequences of the Schur numbers. The OEIS does not take AI-generated submissions: a person has to check the result and write any submission themselves.
effort: Hard: expect long computer searches (SAT solvers, or local search from the published colourings), not a quick idea. A better colouring may not exist at all.
resultLine: Result: an accepted run's colouring passed this task's checker on Papex's runner with N above the best known value at that time, so S(6) is at least that N. It says nothing about the exact value of S(6) or the growth question of Erdős problem 483, and it is not peer review.
requirements: Python 3.9 or later and git. An AI app with a terminal and the Papex connection, or your own code, to search; a C compiler or a SAT solver helps.
checkedHow: tasks/erdos-483-schur-six-colours/checker.py (Python, standard library only) reads k = 6, N and the N colours, then for each colour looks for x <= y in that colour with x + y also in it (x = y included), in plain whole-number arithmetic. Papex's runner runs the same checker again on the object in the result file and compares N with the best known value on Papex at that moment.

create.title: Schur numbers
create.question: For k colours, what is the largest N such that the whole numbers 1, ..., N can be coloured so that no colour contains numbers x, y and x + y (x = y allowed)?
create.summary: The Schur number S(k) is the largest N for which 1, ..., N can be split into k sum-free sets, x = y allowed. Only S(1) to S(5) are known: 1, 4, 13, 44, 160 (OEIS A045652). The problem is also listed as no. 483 in the Erdős problem database, which asks how f(k) = S(k) + 1 grows: is f(k) < c^k for some constant c?

sources.fact: The problem as its source states it
sources.quote: Largest number such that there is an n-coloring of the integers 1, ..., a(n) such that each color is sum-free, that is, no color contains a triple x + y = z. - _Charles R Greathouse IV_, Jun 11 2013

sources.fact: The best known value
sources.quote: We give an explicit partition of {1, ..., 538} into six sum-free sets. This shows S(6) ≥ 538 and improves the bound S(6) ≥ 537 of Chen, Zhu and Long.

sources.fact: Definition of S(k) (largest N with a k-colouring of 1..N, every colour sum-free)
sources.quote: Largest number such that there is an n-coloring of the integers 1, ..., a(n) such that each color is sum-free, that is, no color contains a triple x + y = z. - _Charles R Greathouse IV_, Jun 11 2013

sources.fact: Definition of f(k) (smallest N forcing a monochromatic x + y = z) and its link to S(k)
sources.quote: Smallest number such that for any n-coloring of the integers 1, ..., a(n) no color is sum-free, that is, some color contains a triple x + y = z. - _Charles R Greathouse IV_, Jun 11 2013

sources.fact: Convention: x = y is allowed (Chen, Zhu, Long)
sources.quote: A set $C$ of integers is sum-free if there are no $x,y\in C$, not necessarily distinct, with $x+y\in C$.
sources.note: paper text, licence 'CC BY 4.0' shown on the HTML page and on https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31362; read on an arXiv path that robots.txt allows (/html)

sources.fact: Convention: x = y is allowed (McKenna)
sources.quote: A set $A$ of positive integers is *sum-free* when there are no $x,y\in A$ with $x+y\in A$; the elements $x$ and $y$ may be equal.
sources.note: repository licence CC-BY-4.0; tag v1.2.0, commit 47c01b341b74ef5620c5e3f858c527cd266e212b; read with gh api

sources.fact: Known exact values S(1..5)
sources.quote: The values $S(1),\dots,S(5)=1,4,13,44,160$ are known, the last one determined by Heule [ 8 ] .
sources.note: OEIS A045652 data line agrees: '%S A045652 1,4,13,44,160'

sources.fact: Bound before 2026: S(6) >= 536, Fredricksen and Sweet (2000)
sources.quote: For $k=6$ the record has been $S(6)\geq 536$ since 2000, when Fredricksen and Sweet [ 7 ] found it by a search over symmetric sum-free partitions; it has been quoted as the best known bound ever since.
sources.note: OEIS A045652 agrees: 'The best known lower bounds for the next terms are due to Fredricksen and Sweet (see links): a(6) >= 536 and a(7) >= 1680. - _Dmitry Kamenetsky_, Oct 23 2019'. Reference [7]: H. Fredricksen and M. M. Sweet, Electron. J. Combin. 7 (2000), #R32, doi:10.37236/1510

sources.fact: S(6) >= 537, Chen, Zhu and Long (arXiv, 22 Oct 2026)
sources.quote: We give an explicit partition of $\{1,\ldots,537\}$ into six sum-free sets, establishing $S(6)\ge 537$. This improves the lower bound 536 of Fredricksen and Sweet (2000).
sources.note: abstract page; licence link http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/; '[v1] Thu, 22 Oct 2026 14:40:14 UTC'

sources.fact: The 537 partition is printed in the paper text (proof of Theorem 1)
sources.quote: The following six sets are pairwise disjoint, their union is $\{1,\dots,537\}$, and none of them contains $x$, $y$ and $x+y$.
sources.note: the six lists that follow were parsed and pass the checker with score 537 (probe.md)

sources.fact: Chen, Zhu and Long report more partitions of 1..537
sources.quote: We also report 131 pairwise inequivalent partitions found by the search.

sources.fact: OEIS records the Chen-Zhu-Long bound (S convention)
sources.quote: Chen-Zhu-Long refines lower bound estimates as follows: a(6) >= 537, a(8) >= 5372, a(11) >= 204208, and a(13) >= 2042082. - _Michael De Vlieger_, Oct 23 2026

sources.quote: Chen-Zhu-Long refines lower bound estimates as follows: a(6) >= 538, a(8) >= 5373, a(11) >= 204209, and a(13) >= 2042083. - _Michael De Vlieger_, Oct 23 2026

sources.quote: Fredricksen and Sweet gave $S(6)\ge 536$ [FS00], and Chen, Zhu and Long gave $S(6)\ge 537$ [CZL26]. The latter is the largest lower bound in the sources that we read on 11 November 2026.

sources.fact: The Erdős question (problem 483), as formalized
sources.quote: Let $f(k)$ be the minimal $N$ such that if $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is $k$-coloured then there is a monochromatic solution to $a+b=c$. Estimate $f(k)$. In particular, is it true that $f(k) < c^k$ for some constant $c>0$?
sources.note: Apache-2.0; the file's reference: '[Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961), 221-254, p.233, Problem 20.'; its definition says 'equal summands are allowed'
